scenes.line1: How does Kafka handle message delivery?
scenes.say: Ever wonder how Kafka makes sure your messages arrive, and what happens if they don't?
There are three main delivery guarantees. At-most-once: messages might be lost, but never duplicated. At-least-once: no loss, but you might see duplicates.

scenes.label: Exactly-once
scenes.sub: No loss, no duplicates. Needs transactions.
scenes.say: Exactly-once is the gold standard—no loss, no duplicates. Kafka supports this with transactions and idempotent producers since version zero point eleven.
Pick your delivery semantic based on how critical data loss or duplication is for your app.

scenes.question: How to get exactly-once in Kafka?
scenes.wrong: Just commit the offset after processing.
scenes.right: Enable idempotent producers and use transactions for atomic message and offset commits.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Don't just commit offsets after processing. For exactly-once, you need both idempotent producers and transactions.
